Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Tuesday that the United States is undermining global security by withholding funds from the world’s chemical weapons watchdog, warning that the financial shortfall threatens to halt vital international oversight programs. In a statement posted on X, Araghchi pointed to a November 23 Reuters report detailing how unpaid US dues, or arrears, have pushed the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) into a severe budget crisis. "The U.S. is so concerned about chemical arms that it’s crippling the world’s chemical weapons watchdog," Araghchi wrote, calling Washington's actions "shameful." He warned that the financial strain could force the OPCW to suspend operations and scale back critical initiatives, arguing that the US is "deliberately putting global peace and security at risk" by obstructing the agency's mandate.

🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia seeks missile interceptors around the world The Saudis have reached out to several countries in search of anti-drone weapon systems and missiles, Semafor reports, citing its sources. Among the nations contacted by Saudi Arabia were the US, the UK and France, as well as “countries from the Americas to Asia.” It is unclear whether these inquiries are the result of the Saudi missile interceptor stockpiles running low or a sign of Saudi Arabia preparing for a protracted conflict in the region. During this year, Saudi Arabia came under repeated drone and missile strikes by the Houthis who seek reprisals for the brutal military campaign waged by them and their proxies in Yemen. The Iranian military also carried out missile and attacks against the Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia due to the facility being used by the US forces. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
